newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: BWT earnings weather tough market.
newsitem.headline: BWT earnings weather tough market.

text.p: BWT, Europe's leading water treatment products manufacturer, on Tuesday posted a record batch of 1996 earnings and said further growth would come through its development of new technology.
BWT (Best Water Technology) said group pretax profit jumped 21 percent to 231.1 million schillings ($19.3 million) and sales rose eight percent to 2.32 billion schillings.
"These pleasing results were produced in generally weak economic conditions in Europe," BWT said in a statement.
The group proposed an unchanged dividend of 27 schillings, but will up this to 28 schillings in 1997, chief executive Andreas Weissenbacher told journalists at a news conference on the results.
Water scarcity and an explosion in the world's population provide a basis for future growth, the company said, which it hopes to harness through new technology.
Its efforts will be pinned on a new water treatment technology called "AQA total" that prevents the build-up of lime without the use of chemicals or salt.

BWT expects the new technology, which is primarily aimed at households, to reap extra sales of 200 million schillings in 1998 and to contribute a further 56 million schillings to bottom-line earnings.
Weissenbacher said AQA total was "BWT's theme of the century" and would help make its operations more international.

BWT expects to post higher group sales this year of 2.5 billion after 2.32 billion in 1996 but warned earnings would be hobbled by a 60 million schillings charge needed for marketing and investment in "AQA total".
The first quarter of the current year was running to plan and sales and operating profit would likely show a double-digit percentage gain over the year-ago period, Weissenbacher said.
The share price initially stormed higher in Vienna after the earnings announcement, but then buckled under profit taking. Traders said the record results had largely been within expectations.
BWT stood six schillings lower at 1,626 in midday trade after earlier jumping to 1,665.
The stock has surged 45 percent since the beginning of the year and far outperformed the overall market on the back of expectations of robust profits.
